summary.name: A hierarchy of SRE needs
summary.one_liner: An essay by Liz Fong-Jones proposing a Maslow-style hierarchy of five stages for judging how mature a site reliability engineering (SRE) or DevOps team is.
use_cases: Assessing how mature an SRE or DevOps team is
Deciding what scope an SRE team should own
Arguing for time on projects instead of only operations
Planning SRE hiring and skill mix
Setting boundaries between product development and SRE
summary.what_it_does: The essay argues that SRE organizations differ widely in scope, and that many get stuck doing only the work needed to keep services running. It describes five stages, from physiological health (service works, pager is quiet, outages lead to fixes) through homeostasis, boundaries and objectives, and self-awareness, up to self-actualization (freedom to make substantial design improvements and measure them). It says reaching the higher stages requires both systems and software engineers. It closes with four leadership actions: hire for scaling and reliability expertise, make SRE change the service, give SRE most of its time for projects, and let SRE own the service including saying no to product work. A comment thread adds a view that DevOps belongs in product teams while SRE builds cross-service tooling.
notable: Maslow-inspired five-stage hierarchy for SRE team health
Argues SRE needs both systems and software engineers
Archived copy of a 2016-era Google+ post by Liz Fong-Jones
Author added a note retitling the piece because of the origin of Maslow's concepts
caveats: Opinion essay from around 2015, not a tool or technical specification
